```{r load data}
# Read and clean metadata
meta_data <- read_excel("HotGERMs_SampleSelection.xlsx", sheet = "Sheet2") %>%
  filter(Sequenced == "Yes", Genotype != "BS") %>%
  mutate(
    Biomass_Shoot = as.numeric(`Biomass(Shoot)`),
    Species = if_else(Genotype == "SAP", "Sorghum", "Maize")
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("ID2")

# Read plant expression data
plant_counts <- read.csv("MaizeSorghumOrthologsNormalized.csv", row.names = 1)
plant_pathway <- read.csv("PlantExpression_byKEGGPathway.csv", row.names = 1)
rownames(plant_pathway) <- gsub(" - Zea mays \\(maize\\)", "", rownames(plant_pathway))

# Filter Plant: keep genes with counts >= 250 in more than 3 samples
plant_filtered <- plant_counts %>% 
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>% 
  filter(rowSums(. >= 250) > 3)

# Load gene-to-pathway maps
plant_gene_map <- read.csv("./PlantGene2Pathway.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
microbe_map_A <- read.csv("./AnnotationOutputs/GeneCounts/MicrobeGene2PathwayA.csv")
microbe_map_B <- read.csv("./AnnotationOutputs/GeneCounts/MicrobeGene2PathwayB.csv")

# Function to safely rename long pathway descriptions
simplify_pathways <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(desc_p = case_when(
      str_detect(desc_p, "Biosynthesis of various antibiotics") ~ "Biosynthesis of antibiotics",
      str_detect(desc_p, "Biosynthesis of various other secondary metabolites") ~ "Secondary metabolites biosynthesis A",
      str_detect(desc_p, "Biosynthesis of various plant secondary metabolites") ~ "Secondary metabolites biosynthesis B",
      str_detect(desc_p, "Biosynthesis of various alkaloids") ~ "Alkaloid Biosynthesis",
      str_detect(desc_p, "Biosynthesis of 12-, 14- and 16-membered macrolides") ~ "Macrolides Biosynthesis",
      TRUE ~ desc_p # Keep original if no match
    )) %>%
    # Create the clean gene_taxa identifier immediately
    mutate(name2 = paste0(name, "_", taxa2))
}

microbe_map_A <- simplify_pathways(microbe_map_A)

bacteria_counts <- read.csv("./AnnotationOutputs/GeneCounts/Microbe_Genes_counts.csv", row.names = 1)

# Ensure unique rownames by combining gene name and taxa
bacteria_counts$name2 <- paste0(bacteria_counts$name, "_", bacteria_counts$taxa2)
rownames(bacteria_counts) <- make.unique(bacteria_counts$name2)

# Keep only numeric columns for matrix operations
bacteria_numeric <- bacteria_counts %>% select(where(is.numeric))

# Sum counts for rows that share the same base name (ignoring .1, .2 suffixes)
base_names <- sub("\\.\\d+$", "", rownames(bacteria_numeric))
bacteria_summed <- rowsum(bacteria_numeric, group = base_names)

# Split into two datasets based on filtering thresholds
# 1. All pathways (>= 300 in > 3 samples)
bact_all_filtered <- bacteria_summed %>% filter(rowSums(. >= 100) > 3)

# 2. Focused DAA pathway threshold (>= 50 in > 3 samples)
bact_daa_filtered <- bacteria_summed %>% filter(rowSums(. >= 50) > 3)

# Apply CLR transformation (adding 1 as pseudocount)
bact_all_clr <- as.data.frame(apply(bact_all_filtered + 1, 2, clr))
bact_daa_clr <- as.data.frame(apply(bact_daa_filtered + 1, 2, clr))

# Clean sample names in columns
colnames(bact_all_clr) <- str_remove(colnames(bact_all_clr), "\\.emapper\\.annotations$")
colnames(bact_daa_clr) <- str_remove(colnames(bact_daa_clr), "\\.emapper\\.annotations$")

# Find common samples across Plant and Bacteria datasets
common_cols <- intersect(colnames(plant_filtered), colnames(bact_daa_clr))

# Subset to common columns and convert to matrices
plant_raw <- as.matrix(plant_filtered[, common_cols])
bact_all_raw <- as.matrix(bact_all_clr[, common_cols])
bact_daa_raw <- as.matrix(bact_daa_clr[, common_cols])

# Isolate specific DAA genes from the DAA matrix
daa_gene_list <- read.csv("DAAGenes_EC.csv")
daa_map <- microbe_map_A %>% filter(name %in% daa_gene_list$name)

bact_daa_raw <- bact_daa_raw[rownames(bact_daa_raw) %in% daa_map$name2, ]

# Create scaled matrices for distance/regression analyses (Mantel, PERMANOVA)
# Unscaled matrices (plant_raw, bact_daa_raw) remain available for Networks/Random Forests
plant_scaled <- scale(plant_raw, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
bact_daa_scaled <- scale(bact_daa_raw, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
bact_all_scaled <- scale(bact_all_raw, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)

# Quick validation check:
cat("Plant Matrix Dimensions:", dim(plant_raw), "\n")
cat("Microbe DAA Matrix Dimensions:", dim(bact_daa_raw), "\n")
```

```{r global tree}
# Extract all unique raw taxa from the global dataset
all_taxa_raw <- data.frame(row_info = rownames(bact_all_raw)) %>%
  separate(row_info, into = c("Gene", "Taxon"), sep = "_", extra = "merge") %>%
  mutate(CleanTaxon = trimws(str_to_lower(str_remove_all(Taxon, "[0-9_]")))) %>%
  pull(CleanTaxon) %>%
  unique()

# Query NCBI for their Family rank
# NOTE: If this times out due to NCBI limits, run it once, save it with saveRDS(), 
# and load it back in subsequent runs.
cat("Querying NCBI for global family ranks...\n")
get_family_safe <- function(tax_string) {
  Sys.sleep(0.4) # Pause for 400 milliseconds
  
  # tryCatch prevents the whole loop from crashing if one single microbe fails
  tryCatch({
    taxize::tax_name(sci = tax_string, get = "family", db = "ncbi", rows = 1)
  }, error = function(e) {
    # If a network error happens, return an NA row to keep the structure intact
    data.frame(db = "ncbi", query = tax_string, family = NA, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
}

# 2. Run the slow function over your list of taxa
global_families_list <- lapply(all_taxa_raw, get_family_safe)

# 3. Bind the results back into a single dataframe
global_families <- bind_rows(global_families_list)

cat("Finished querying NCBI!\n")

#Number of families
global_families %>%
  filter(!is.na(family)) %>%
  pull(family) %>%
  n_distinct()

#  Clean up the list of families (remove NAs and format)
clean_global_families <- global_families %>%
  filter(!is.na(family)) %>%
  pull(family) %>%
  str_to_title() %>%
  unique()

cat("Fetching full NCBI taxonomic lineages for", length(clean_global_families), "families...\n")

bad_families <- c("amelidae", "orobanchaceae", "diapheromeridae", "lampyridae", "pseudococcidae", "proteidae", "bacillidae","nectriaceae", "saccharomycetaceae", "chaetomiaceae", "arthrodermataceae", "hypocreaceae", "sordariaceae", "debaryomycetaceae", "clavicipitaceae")

clean_global_families <- clean_global_families[!tolower(clean_global_families) %in% bad_families]
# Get the full lineage (Kingdom -> Phylum -> Class -> Order -> Family) for each
# Note: This sends a batch query to NCBI. It may take 30-60 seconds.
ncbi_class <- taxize::classification(clean_global_families, db = "ncbi")



# 2. Check for any families that NCBI couldn't resolve (should be 0 since we validated them earlier)
missing_class <- is.na(ncbi_class)
if(any(missing_class)) {
  cat("Warning: Could not fetch lineages for:", paste(names(ncbi_class)[missing_class], collapse=", "), "\n")
  # Filter out the missing ones so the tree builder doesn't crash
  ncbi_class <- ncbi_class[!missing_class]
}

# Convert the list of lineages into a taxonomic tree
# This function calculates a distance matrix based on shared taxonomic ranks
cat("Building taxonomic tree...\n")
tax_tree <- taxize::class2tree(ncbi_class)

# 4. Extract the 'phylo' object
global_phylo <- tax_tree$phylo

# 5. Save the tree to upload to iTOL
ape::write.tree(global_phylo, file = "Global_Microbial_Families_NCBI.tre")
cat("Success! Taxonomic tree saved to Global_Microbial_Families_NCBI.tre\n")

# Quick check of the tree size
cat("Number of tips on the new tree:", length(global_phylo$tip.label), "\n")
```

```{r differential correlations}
# Ensure the column name matches your metadata (e.g., "Temperature")
samples_28 <- rownames(meta_data)[meta_data$Temp == 28 & rownames(meta_data) %in% colnames(plant_raw)]
samples_38 <- rownames(meta_data)[meta_data$Temp == 38 & rownames(meta_data) %in% colnames(plant_raw)]

# Transpose the data matrices so genes are columns and samples are rows (required by cor())
Plant_28 <- t(plant_raw[, samples_28])
Microbe_28 <- t(bact_daa_raw[, samples_28])

Plant_38 <- t(plant_raw[, samples_38])
Microbe_38 <- t(bact_daa_raw[, samples_38])

cat("28°C Samples n =", nrow(Plant_28), "| 38°C Samples n =", nrow(Plant_38), "\n")

# Compute Spearman correlations
cor_28 <- cor(Plant_28, Microbe_28, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
cor_38 <- cor(Plant_38, Microbe_38, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Melt to long format
cor_28_df <- reshape2::melt(cor_28, varnames = c("PlantGene", "MicrobeGene"), value.name = "cor_28")
cor_38_df <- reshape2::melt(cor_38, varnames = c("PlantGene", "MicrobeGene"), value.name = "cor_38")

# Merge and compute Fisher z-transformed difference
diff_cor_results <- full_join(cor_28_df, cor_38_df, by = c("PlantGene", "MicrobeGene")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Safety catch to prevent infinite Z-scores if correlation is perfectly 1 or -1
    cor_28 = case_when(cor_28 >= 1 ~ 0.9999, cor_28 <= -1 ~ -0.9999, TRUE ~ cor_28),
    cor_38 = case_when(cor_38 >= 1 ~ 0.9999, cor_38 <= -1 ~ -0.9999, TRUE ~ cor_38),
    
    z_28 = atanh(cor_28),  
    z_38 = atanh(cor_38),
    diff_z = z_38 - z_28,
    se = sqrt(1 / (nrow(Plant_28) - 3) + 1 / (nrow(Plant_38) - 3)),
    z_score = diff_z / se,
    p_value = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z_score)),
    FDR = p.adjust(p_value, method = "fdr")
  )

# Filter for significant differential correlations (FDR < 0.05)
sig_diff <- diff_cor_results %>% filter(FDR < 0.05)

cat("Found", nrow(sig_diff), "significant differential correlations between 28°C and 38°C.\n")
```

```{r collapse2family and count}
# Aggregate the differential correlation values for each microbe gene
daa_gene_stats <- sig_diff %>%
  group_by(MicrobeGene) %>%
  summarise(
    # Average differential shift across all significant plant interactions for this gene
    Mean_Diff_Z = mean(diff_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    Sig_Edges = n() 
  ) %>%
  # Split the MicrobeGene name back into Gene and Taxon
  separate(MicrobeGene, into = c("Gene", "Taxon"), sep = "_", extra = "merge") %>%
  mutate(CleanTaxon = trimws(str_to_lower(str_remove_all(Taxon, "[0-9_]"))))

# Map the taxa to their NCBI families (using global_families generated earlier)
daa_family_stats <- daa_gene_stats %>%
  left_join(global_families, by = c("CleanTaxon" = "query")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(family)) %>%
  mutate(Family = str_to_title(family))

# Aggregate up to the Family level
# If multiple taxa in the same family have the same gene, we average their correlation shifts
daa_heatmap_data <- daa_family_stats %>%
  group_by(Family, Gene) %>%
  summarise(Plot_Value = mean(Mean_Diff_Z, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Pivot wider: Rows = Families (Tree Leaves), Columns = DAA Genes (Heatmap Boxes)
  pivot_wider(names_from = Gene, values_from = Plot_Value)

cat("Aggregated family-level heatmap data dimensions:", dim(daa_heatmap_data), "\n")

# Optional: write to CSV
# write.csv(final_family_summary, "DAA_FamilyLevel_DiffCor.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r generate itol annotation file}
# 1. Categorize each significant gene as favoring 28C or 38C, then count them per family
daa_bar_data <- daa_family_stats %>%
  mutate(Favored_Temp = ifelse(Mean_Diff_Z > 0, "Stronger_at_38C", "Stronger_at_28C")) %>%
  group_by(Family, Favored_Temp) %>%
  summarise(Gene_Count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Pivot so we have columns for the 28C counts and 38C counts
  pivot_wider(names_from = Favored_Temp, values_from = Gene_Count, values_fill = list(Gene_Count = 0))

# Safety check: Ensure both columns exist just in case the data is heavily skewed
if(!"Stronger_at_38C" %in% colnames(daa_bar_data)) daa_bar_data$Stronger_at_38C <- 0
if(!"Stronger_at_28C" %in% colnames(daa_bar_data)) daa_bar_data$Stronger_at_28C <- 0

# 2. Define the iTOL Multi-Bar Header
itol_bar_header <- c(
  "DATASET_MULTIBAR",
  "SEPARATOR COMMA",
  "DATASET_LABEL,Significant_Gene_Counts",
  "COLOR,#000000",
  
  # Define the labels and colors for the bars
  "FIELD_LABELS,Stronger at 28C,Stronger at 38C",
  "FIELD_COLORS,#3C1A42F,#ED4E3EF", # Blue for 28C, Red for 38C
  
  # iTOL specific multi-bar settings
  "ALIGN_FIELDS,1",       # 1 = Start bars from the same baseline
  "DATASET_SCALE,1",      # Show a numeric scale 
  "MARGIN,5",             # Space between tree leaves and bars
  
  "DATA"
)

# 3. Format the data rows
bar_lines <- apply(daa_bar_data, 1, function(row) {
  # Paste Family, Count_28, Count_38
  paste(row["Family"], row["Stronger_at_28C"], row["Stronger_at_38C"], sep = ",")
})

# 4. Export the file
writeLines(c(itol_bar_header, bar_lines), "iTOL_DAA_MultiBar_Temp.txt")
cat("Success! Bar chart annotation saved to iTOL_DAA_MultiBar_Temp.txt\n")
```


```{r labelTree2}
#  Extract the 'Class' rank from the ncbi_class object
cat("Extracting Class taxonomy for each family...\n")

class_mapping <- lapply(names(ncbi_class), function(tax_name) {
  tax_df <- ncbi_class[[tax_name]]
  if (is.data.frame(tax_df)) {
    class_row <- tax_df[tax_df$rank == "class", ]
    if (nrow(class_row) > 0) {
      return(data.frame(Family = tax_name, Class = str_to_title(class_row$name[1])))
    }
  }
  return(data.frame(Family = tax_name, Class = "Unknown"))
})

class_df <- bind_rows(class_mapping) %>% mutate(Family = str_to_title(Family))

# Assign the VIRIDIS color scale
unique_classes <- unique(class_df$Class)
# Base R natively supports viridis!
class_colors <- setNames(hcl.colors(length(unique_classes), palette = "viridis"), unique_classes)

# --- FILE 1: THE BRANCH COLORS ---
itol_branch_header <- c(
  "TREE_COLORS",
  "SEPARATOR COMMA",
  "DATA"
)

# Format: NODE_ID, TYPE, COLOR, STYLE, SIZE_FACTOR
branch_lines <- apply(class_df, 1, function(row) {
  paste(row["Family"], "branch", class_colors[row["Class"]], "normal", "2", sep = ",")
})

writeLines(c(itol_branch_header, branch_lines), "iTOL_Viridis_Branches.txt")


# Extract the 'Class' rank (Same as before)
class_mapping <- lapply(names(ncbi_class), function(tax_name) {
  tax_df <- ncbi_class[[tax_name]]
  if (is.data.frame(tax_df)) {
    class_row <- tax_df[tax_df$rank == "class", ]
    if (nrow(class_row) > 0) {
      return(data.frame(Family = tax_name, Class = str_to_title(class_row$name[1])))
    }
  }
  return(data.frame(Family = tax_name, Class = "Unknown"))
})

class_df <- bind_rows(class_mapping) %>% mutate(Family = str_to_title(Family))

# Assign the VIRIDIS color scale for the font
unique_classes <- unique(class_df$Class)
class_colors <- setNames(hcl.colors(length(unique_classes), palette = "viridis"), unique_classes)

# Create the iTOL TEXT DATASET header
itol_text_header <- c(
  "DATASET_TEXT",
  "SEPARATOR COMMA",
  "DATASET_LABEL,Class_Names",
  "COLOR,#000000",
  
  # iTOL Text Alignment Settings
  "ALIGN_TO_LABELS,1",     # Aligns the text flush outside the tree
  "LABEL_ROTATION,0",      # Keeps text readable (horizontal)
  
  "DATA"
)

# Format the data rows
# iTOL Format: NODE_ID, LABEL_TEXT, POSITION, COLOR, STYLE, SIZE_FACTOR, ROTATION
# We use POSITION = -1 (outside the tree), STYLE = 'bold', and SIZE = 1.5 to make it pop.
text_lines <- apply(class_df, 1, function(row) {
  fam <- row["Family"]
  cls <- row["Class"]
  hex_col <- class_colors[cls]
  
  paste(fam, cls, "-1", hex_col, "bold", "1.5", "0", sep = ",")
})

# Export the file
writeLines(c(itol_text_header, text_lines), "iTOL_Class_Text.txt")
cat("Success! Text label annotation saved to iTOL_Class_Text.txt\n")

```



```{r global_expression_activity}
# Map all globally expressed genes to their taxonomic families
#bact_all_df <- as.data.frame(bact_all_raw)

#Let's look at just one microbiome treatment
field_cols <- intersect(colnames(bact_all_raw), rownames(meta_data)[meta_data$Soil == "Field"])
bact_all_df <- as.data.frame(bact_all_raw[, field_cols])
bact_all_df$RowInfo <- rownames(bact_all_df)

# Pivot long to easily parse out the taxonomy
bact_all_long <- bact_all_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -RowInfo, names_to = "Sample", values_to = "CLR_Value") %>%
  separate(RowInfo, into = c("Gene", "Taxon"), sep = "_", extra = "merge") %>%
  mutate(CleanTaxon = trimws(str_to_lower(str_remove_all(Taxon, "[0-9_]"))))

# Join with the global_families classification table
family_expression <- bact_all_long %>%
  left_join(global_families, by = c("CleanTaxon" = "query")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(family)) %>%
  mutate(Family = str_to_title(family))

# 2. Aggregate expression at the family level
# We take the mean CLR of all genes within a family for each sample to represent "Total Activity"
family_sample_activity <- family_expression %>%
  group_by(Family, Sample) %>%
  summarise(
    Family_Mean_CLR = mean(CLR_Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Genes_Identified = n_distinct(Gene), 
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 3. Add temperature metadata and filter for our samples of interest
family_sample_activity <- family_sample_activity %>%
  mutate(Temp = case_when(
    Sample %in% samples_38 ~ "38C",
    Sample %in% samples_28 ~ "28C",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  )) %>%
  filter(Temp %in% c("28C", "38C"))

# 4. Perform differential analysis (T-Test) for each family
family_activity_stats <- family_sample_activity %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  # Safety catch: Ensure there are enough samples in both groups to run a t-test
  filter(sum(Temp == "28C") >= 3 & sum(Temp == "38C") >= 3) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_28 = mean(Family_Mean_CLR[Temp == "28C"], na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_38 = mean(Family_Mean_CLR[Temp == "38C"], na.rm = TRUE),
    p_val = wilcox.test(Family_Mean_CLR[Temp == "38C"], Family_Mean_CLR[Temp == "28C"], exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    diff = mean_38 - mean_28,
    # Define enrichment status based on p < 0.05
    Status = case_when(
      p_val < 0.05 & diff > 0 ~ "Enriched_38C",
      p_val < 0.05 & diff < 0 ~ "Enriched_28C",
      TRUE ~ "No_Change"
    )
  )

cat("--- Global Family Activity Shifts (p < 0.05) ---\n")
print(table(family_activity_stats$Status))
cat("----------------------------------------------\n")

# 5. Generate iTOL Color Strip Annotation
# Define colors: Red for 38C, Blue for 28C, Light Grey for No Change
status_colors <- c(
  "Enriched_38C" = "#F4815A",
  "Enriched_28C" = "#5ACCAD",
  "No_Change" = "gray80" 
)

itol_activity_header <- c(
  "DATASET_COLORSTRIP",
  "SEPARATOR COMMA",
  "DATASET_LABEL,Global_Activity_Shift",
  "COLOR,#000000",
  "STRIP_WIDTH,30",        # Distinct thickness 
  "COLOR_BRANCHES,0",
  "SHOW_LABELS,0",         # Set to 0 so we just see the clean block of color
  "DATA"
)

# Format the rows: Family, Hex Color, Text Label
activity_lines <- apply(family_activity_stats, 1, function(row) {
  fam <- row["Family"]
  status <- row["Status"]
  hex_col <- status_colors[status]
  
  # iTOL will ignore NA families automatically
  if(!is.na(hex_col)) {
    paste(fam, hex_col, status, sep = ",")
  }
})

# Remove any empty rows
activity_lines <- unlist(activity_lines)

# Export the file
writeLines(c(itol_activity_header, activity_lines), "iTOL_Global_Activity_ColorStrip.txt")
cat("Success! Global activity color strip saved to iTOL_Global_Activity_ColorStrip.txt\n")
```



Make Violin plot from public data
```{r}
SuppTable<-read.csv("./LiteratureData/Knight_level4Models.csv")
daaECs<-read.csv("./DAAGenes_EC.csv")


flag_T <- grepl("\\(T\\)$", SuppTable$level4)
# Extract EC numbers
SuppTable$EC <- sub(".*\\(EC ([0-9\\.]+)\\).*", "\\1", SuppTable$level4)
SuppTable$EC[!grepl("\\(EC", SuppTable$level4)] <- NA

SuppTable$D_AA_pathway <- flag_T | (SuppTable$EC %in% daaECs$pathway_EC)

# Survey all level1 categories (excluding our special D-AA genes)
pathway_survey <- SuppTable %>%
  filter(!is.na(level1) & D_AA_pathway == FALSE) %>%
  group_by(level1) %>%
  # Filter out categories with too few genes to run a t-test
  filter(n() >= 3) %>% 
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean_Effect_H = mean(estimate_TreatmentH, na.rm = TRUE),
    p_val = t.test(estimate_TreatmentH, mu = 0)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Significance = case_when(
      p_val < 0.05 & Mean_Effect_H > 0 ~ "Increased (+)",
      p_val < 0.05 & Mean_Effect_H < 0 ~ "Decreased (-)",
      TRUE ~ "No Change (0)"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Mean_Effect_H))

plot_data <- SuppTable %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(
    D_AA_pathway == TRUE ~ "D-AA Pathway",
    level1 == "Amino Acids and Derivatives" ~ "Amino Acids and Derivatives",
    level1 == "Carbohydrates" ~ "Carbohydrates",
    level1 == "Dormancy and Sporulation" ~ "Dormancy and Sporulation",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  filter(!is.na(group))

# Define the exact target order we want left-to-right
target_order <- c("D-AA Pathway", 
                  "Amino Acids and Derivatives", 
                  "Carbohydrates",
                  "Dormancy and Sporulation")

# Apply factor to group for the ANOVA and Fill Colors
plot_data$group <- factor(plot_data$group, levels = target_order)

anova_model <- aov(estimate_TreatmentH ~ group, data = plot_data)

# Run Fisher's LSD
lsd_results <- LSD.test(anova_model, "group", group = TRUE)

# Extract letters
letters_df <- data.frame(
  group = as.character(rownames(lsd_results$groups)),
  Letter = as.character(lsd_results$groups$groups),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Calculate N and Max Y, join letters
letter_placement_df <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Max_Y = max(estimate_TreatmentH, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(letters_df, by = "group") %>%
  mutate(
    New_Label = paste0(group, "\n(n = ", N, ")")
  )

# ---> BULLETPROOF X-AXIS ORDERING <---
# Force the summary dataframe to sort exactly by our target_order
letter_placement_df <- letter_placement_df %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = target_order)) %>%
  arrange(group)

# Join the newly generated labels back to the main data
plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  left_join(select(letter_placement_df, group, New_Label), by = "group")

# Lock in the X-axis levels using the perfectly sorted letter_placement_df
plot_data$New_Label <- factor(plot_data$New_Label, levels = letter_placement_df$New_Label)

y_offset <- max(letter_placement_df$Max_Y, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.08 

# Generate the plot
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = New_Label, y = estimate_TreatmentH, fill = group)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE) +
  theme_classic() +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, fill = "white", outlier.shape = NA) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#f9785d", "#7c2382ff","#331067","#fecd90ff")) +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = "Heat Stress Effect") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none", 
        text = element_text(size = 18, family = "sans")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = letter_placement_df, 
            aes(x = New_Label, y = Max_Y + y_offset, label = Letter), 
            size = 7, fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE)

ggsave("./Figures/DistributionofHeatStressEffectFromNatureSoil2.pdf",width=5,height=7)
```
